title: en el administrador de teclado, algunos atajos no me funcionan

status.label: Reproduce Keyboard Manager shortcut failures
status.detail: The original report describes Win+Pause and Shift+VolumeUp failures; a later user reports a separate shortcut-to-shortcut mapping failure on PowerToys 0.93.

judgment.rationale: The original report gives concrete non-working mappings and says one failing shortcut can stop other shortcut remaps. A later commenter describes a separate Ctrl+Alt+X-to-Win+Shift+Arrow failure on PowerToys 0.93 while a text action works. These reports establish a reproducible class of shortcut-remap failures, but do not prove a single root cause or that the original reporter's old mappings remain affected.
evidence: The original report on PowerToys 0.81.1 maps Win+Pause to Ctrl+Numpad0 and reports that Windows System Information still opens.
The original report also says Shift+VolumeUp fails and that other shortcut mappings stop responding after using a failing mapping.
A later commenter reports Ctrl+Alt+X mapped to Win+Shift+Arrow failing on PowerToys 0.93 while Shift+F12-to-text works.
Issue #28031 is a broader older browser-remapping report, but it does not establish the same shortcut endpoint or failure mechanism.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce the newer shortcut-to-shortcut case separately from the original Win+Pause and volume-key mappings, then identify whether system-reserved or special keys bypass shortcut dispatch.

fix_assessment.rationale: If the supplied cases reproduce, Keyboard Manager should consistently intercept and dispatch configured shortcuts without losing unrelated mappings. The issue includes distinct endpoint types, so a shared cause must not be assumed.

proposed_fixes.title: Preserve dispatch for shortcut-to-shortcut mappings
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Some source or destination chords may be intercepted by Windows or treated differently by Keyboard Manager, potentially preventing the configured action and leaving later mappings unresponsive; this is an unconfirmed hypothesis.
plan: Reproduce the current Ctrl+Alt+X-to-Win+Shift+Arrow mapping and test the original Win+Pause and Shift+VolumeUp mappings separately.
Compare shortcut-to-shortcut remapping with the working text action and capture whether the source chord reaches Keyboard Manager and whether the destination chord is emitted.
Determine whether OS-reserved or special multimedia keys require a distinct dispatch path before selecting a shared fix.
Add focused regression tests for each confirmed failing endpoint and ensure other mappings remain active.
verification: Each confirmed mapping performs its configured action without invoking the original OS action.
A failing or unsupported mapping does not disable unrelated shortcut mappings.
Text remapping and ordinary shortcut mappings continue to work.

confidence.rationale: A detailed PowerToys 0.93 shortcut-to-shortcut failure and an older report with specific mappings support investigation, but the reports may represent distinct bugs and no maintainer reproduction is documented.

issue_context.summary: Several Keyboard Manager shortcut mappings reportedly fail, with examples spanning OS-reserved, multimedia, and shortcut-to-shortcut endpoints.
known_information: The original issue reports PowerToys 0.81.1 and Win+Pause-to-Ctrl+Numpad0 plus Shift+VolumeUp failures.
The original report says a failing mapping can be followed by other shortcut mappings no longer responding.
A later comment reports on PowerToys 0.93 that Ctrl+Alt+X-to-Win+Shift+Arrow fails while Shift+F12-to-text works.
The later comment is a separate report and does not establish the original reporter's current behavior.
inferences: The cases may involve different shortcut endpoints or OS interception rather than one shared dispatch defect.
issue_context.analysis: The 0.93 report supplies a current, specific reproduction candidate, while the original cases include Windows-reserved and volume-key combinations. They should be tested independently before grouping them under a single fix.
initial_investigation: Read the Spanish issue body and both comments, including the later PowerToys 0.93 report.
Reviewed #28031, a broad older Spanish report about Keyboard Manager remapping in browsers; it does not establish coverage for these shortcut-to-shortcut mappings.
No maintainer reproduction or current confirmation from the original reporter is present.

information_gaps.information: Whether the original Win+Pause and Shift+VolumeUp mappings still fail on current stable, and whether the later Ctrl+Alt+X report remains reproducible
information_gaps.why_needed: The report combines old original examples with a later user's different mapping; current confirmation prevents treating unrelated failures as one defect.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Ask the original reporter to confirm the two original mappings on current stable; ask the commenter who supplied the 0.93 case to confirm its exact mapping and current behavior.

comment.body: This issue includes your Win+Pause and Shift+VolumeUp examples, plus a later report of Ctrl+Alt+X mapped to Win+Shift+Arrow failing on PowerToys 0.93. Could you confirm whether your original mappings still fail on current stable? The commenter who supplied the 0.93 case could also confirm whether that exact mapping still reproduces.

reproduce.title: Test shortcut dispatch independently for each mapping
prerequisites: Use each mapping as a separate test
setup: Where available, configure Ctrl+Alt+X to send Win+Shift+Arrow.
Separately test Win+Pause to Ctrl+Numpad0 and Shift+VolumeUp.
steps: Trigger one configured shortcut and record whether its destination action occurs and whether the original OS action also occurs.
Trigger an unrelated working shortcut mapping, including Shift+F12-to-text when reproducing the commenter case.
Repeat each mapping independently and note whether one failed mapping affects the others.
reproduce.expected_result: Each supported mapping performs only its configured action, and a failure in one mapping does not disable unrelated mappings.
